record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: A comparability graph is an undirected graph whose edges can be oriented so that whenever (u, v) and (v, w) are directed edges, (u, w) is also a directed edge. For a graph class F and integer p, F - pe denotes graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by adding at most p edges, and F + pv denotes graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by deleting at most p vertices. What is the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of Coloring on comparability - pe graphs and on comparability + pv graphs?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10 Determine the complexity of Coloring for the classes of comparability−pe graphs and comparability+pv graphs when parameterized by p.
An (undirected) graph is a comparability graph if there exists an assignment of exactly one direction to each of its edges

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An undirected simple graph G is called a comparability graph if each of its edges can be assigned a direction so that whenever (u,v) and (v,w) are directed edges of the resulting orientation, (u,w) is also a directed edge (i.e., the orientation is transitive). For a class of graphs F and a non-negative integer p, define:
- F − pe = { G : there exists a set E' of at most p edges of G such that G − E' ∈ F }, i.e., graphs obtainable from a member of F by adding at most p edges; equivalently, graphs that become a member of F after deleting at most p edges.
- F + pv = { G : there exists a set S of at most p vertices of G such that G − S ∈ F }, i.e., graphs from which one can delete at most p vertices to obtain a graph in F.

The Coloring problem asks, given a graph H and an integer k, whether H admits a proper k-coloring (an assignment of colors 1,…,k to vertices such that adjacent vertices receive distinct colors), where the chromatic number is to be determined.

Let F be the class of comparability graphs. Determine the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of the Coloring problem on the graph classes F − pe and F + pv. In particular, decide whether Coloring on each of these classes is fixed-parameter tractable, in XP, W[1]-hard, or para-NP-hard when parameterized by p.
artifact.status_search_result: Coloring on comparability graphs is polynomial-time solvable. For the modified classes, partial results are known: Coloring on comparability+1e and comparability−1e graphs is polynomial-time solvable, while for fixed k ≥ 2, Coloring on comparability+ke graphs is NP-complete (Takenaga–Higashide). The full parameterized-complexity classification with parameter p (FPT vs. W[1]-hard, etc.) for both comparability−pe and comparability+pv does not appear to be settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Vertex Coloring of Comparability+ke and -ke Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Vertex coloring of comparability+ke graphs is polynomial for k=1 and NP-complete for k≥2; vertex coloring of comparability-1e graphs is polynomial.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for the edge-modification variant but not a full parameterized-complexity classification.

status_evidence.title: The complexity of comparability graph recognition and coloring
status_evidence.snippet: Coloring on comparability graphs is polynomial-time solvable.
status_evidence.claim: Base class admits polynomial coloring, motivating the parameterized question for nearby classes.
